speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth how does the new Singapore Government Partnerships Office plan to build and maintain respectful, age-appropriate and on-going partnerships with children and young people under 18 years old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: These proposals would then be referred accordingly to Government agencies which would work in partnership with these citizens to realise their proposals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I welcome the opportunity made available to young people over the age of 18.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: My concern here is: how are we getting inputs from our young people?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: So, my supplementary questions are, if the Ministry is not in a position to engage directly with children and young people under 18 years of age, how does the Ministry tend to ensure that the views of children and young people are known and considered by the partnerships office?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: My second question is: would the Ministry consider working with children and young people under 18 years of age, parents and guardians, schools and sporting and community groups to scope possible mechanisms to ensure that the views of children and young people are known and considered by the partnerships office?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, like the Member, we want to ensure that there is meaningful inclusion as well as consideration of children and young persons' views and perspectives.
